defect.evidence_quote: we adopted the general rule that a constitutional error does not automatically require reversal of a conviction
defect.problem: The holding is substantively supported, but the text trails off at 'not automatic…' instead of stating the completed rule.
defect.proposed_fix: Complete the holding as: admission of an involuntary/coerced confession is trial error subject to Chapman harmless-error analysis, not automatic reversal.

reasons: The opinion says a majority found coerced confessions subject to harmless-error analysis.
The Court characterizes admission of an involuntary confession as a classic trial error and says review asks whether admission was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Also mention the case-specific result: the admitted confession was not harmless on these facts.

reasons: The opinion repeatedly frames the case as a due-process voluntariness/coerced-confession case under the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments.
The opinion refines confession doctrine by holding a credible threat may coerce a confession and by treating admitted coerced confessions as trial error subject to harmless-error review.
The lake progeny data shows extensive later citation, supporting the 'Key' characterization.
